correctness.rationale: The primary theorem makes every nonzero-weight operator on the odd-dimensional simple bilinear-form Jordan algebra splitting. Example 13 reduces every nontrivial J_3(f) operator, up to R↦-R-Delta I, to rank one with a two-dimensional unital kernel and an isotropic one-dimensional image. The image lines form a nonsingular projective conic with q+1 points; for each image line exactly q of the q+1 unital two-dimensional subalgebras are complementary. This gives q(q+1) rank-one operators and, by the involution, the same number of rank-two operators, plus the two trivial operators. The package checker independently exhausts all 3^9 endomorphisms for both binary-form classes over F_3 and directly replays the construction for F_5, F_7, and F_11.

value.rationale: The primary classification leaves a natural finite-field moduli question: how many of the splitting projections actually occur and how they distribute by rank. The answer is uniform across both Witt types, has a simple conic-times-complement interpretation, and determines all extension-field point counts and a closed zeta function. This is a natural exact invariant of the complete classified locus rather than an arbitrary parameter slice.
